summary: Temporal server's Elasticsearch cluster settings configuration globally disables `action.auto_create_index`, breaking existing Elasticsearch clusters that rely on automatic index creation. The setting should be scoped to only Temporal indices.
userImpact: Users deploying Temporal with Elasticsearch visibility store experience broken auto-index creation for all indices in the cluster, not just Temporal indices.
rootCause: The Elasticsearch cluster settings configuration applies `action.auto_create_index: false` globally across the cluster instead of scoping it to Temporal visibility indices only.
proposedFix: Scope the auto_create_index setting to Temporal indices only using pattern matching: `"action.auto_create_index": "-temporal_visibility_v1*,+*"` to disable it only for Temporal indices while allowing it for others.
resolutionDetails: The Helm chart was updated to stop applying cluster settings by default, preventing the global override of the action.auto_create_index setting (temporalio/helm-charts#901).
keyQuote: Even if I start elasticsearch using the ECK option `action.auto_create_index: true`, temporal overrides that.
